findings.title: bwrap `--chdir "$PWD"` hard-fails when CWD is under /tmp
findings.desc: The sandbox mounts a tmpfs over /tmp and only re-exposes $AE on top of it, so if the caller's working directory is anywhere under /tmp, `--chdir "$PWD"` targets a path that doesn't exist in the sandbox and bwrap errors out with no fallback (the probe already passed). The probe omits the $AE bind and the --chdir despite the comment claiming it uses the "SAME mounts the real run uses", so this is precisely the probe-passes-but-run-fails case the comment says was fixed.

findings.title: np.load positional allow_pickle now fails open
findings.desc: The 3rd-positional check only rejects a truthy *literal*, so `np.load(f, None, flag)` with a variable set to True passes the gate — a pickle-RCE path the previous check caught, and inconsistent with the keyword `allow_pickle` check directly below, which fails closed on anything non-literal. Runtime containment is the stated boundary, but on the resource-limits-only tier that boundary is documented as best-effort.

findings.title: Vacuous assertion in writes-contained test
findings.desc: `grep -qiE 'contained at runtime|runtime'` matches any file containing the word "runtime" anywhere, so the second assertion can never fail and adds no verification signal to a security-guard test.

findings.title: "os/subprocess are import-blocked" overlooks attribute-reachable os
findings.desc: `os` remains reachable as an attribute of approved modules (e.g. `pandas.os`, `numpy.os`), so dropping `system`/`popen`/`fork`/`exec*` from BAD_ATTRS lets `pd.os.system(...)` pass the static gate. On the bwrap tier confine.py is not in the invocation, so exec actually occurs inside the sandbox (no net, ro rootfs — contained, but the comment's claim that import-blocking plus confine.py covers this is inaccurate for that tier).

findings.title: bwrap probe does not use the real mount set
findings.desc: The comment says the probe uses "the SAME mounts the real run uses," but it omits `--ro-bind "$AE" "$AE"`, `--chdir`, `--new-session`, and `--clearenv`. A host that fails only on the real configuration (e.g. tmpfs-overlay bind denied) will still hard-fail at run time instead of degrading, which is exactly what the probe exists to prevent (the decision doc repeats the claim at docs/decisions/019-arithmetic-eval-sandboxing.md:55-56).

findings.title: Vacuous grep alternation makes assertion unfailable
findings.desc: `grep -qiE 'contained at runtime|runtime'` matches any SKILL.md containing the word "runtime" anywhere, so the second assertion in "filesystem writes are contained at runtime" can never fail. Drop the bare `|runtime` alternative.

findings.title: Stale "write methods are blocked below" claim on pathlib
findings.desc: The check.py header comment says pathlib's write methods are "blocked below and at runtime," but no static block for pathlib write methods exists in the gate (BAD_ATTRS contains none, and the design/docs state writes are runtime-only). The comment overstates static coverage.

findings.title: "Prefer absolute paths" rationale doesn't follow
findings.desc: Under bwrap the CWD is the caller's real `$PWD` (via `--chdir "$PWD"`), and its read-only-ness does not affect relative-path *reads*; the claim that a moved data file will "fail cleanly rather than silently" because of the read-only mount is muddled. The advice may be fine, but the stated mechanism is wrong.

findings.title: Non-bwrap process containment is bypassable

The documentation misleadingly singles out only the resource-limit fallback as unsafe despite the unshare tier relying on the same best-effort Python confinement for filesystem and process isolation.

findings.title: bwrap fails when the working directory is under `/tmp`

findings.title: tmpfs mount can shadow `--chdir "$PWD"` under bwrap
findings.desc: The bwrap invocation mounts a fresh `--tmpfs /tmp` and then re-exposes only `$AE` read-only on top of it (to avoid shadowing), but does **not** re-expose `$PWD`. If the caller's working directory is itself under `/tmp` (a common case, e.g. CI workspaces or `TMPDIR`-based project dirs), the new tmpfs will shadow it, so `--chdir "$PWD"` lands in an empty writable tmpfs instead of the real, read-only working directory — contradicting the documented invariant that "CWD stays the caller's dir (read-only) so relative data reads work."

findings.title: Static open()-write-mode gate removed, weakening the already-weak fallback tier
findings.desc: `check.py` previously fail-closed on any `open()` call whose mode wasn't a literal read mode; this diff removes that check entirely, relying solely on runtime containment. The unchanged `confine.py` only guards specific `os.*` functions (remove/unlink/rename/mkdir/...) and does not intercept the builtin `open()`, so on the "resource-limits-only fallback" tier (which the ADR itself calls best-effort and warns should not run untrusted scripts) this diff removes a previously-working static defense-in-depth layer against arbitrary file writes without adding an equivalent runtime replacement for that tier.

findings.title: check.py evaluates payload natively on host
findings.desc: The bash condition `if python3 "$AE/check.py" "$AE/script.py"; then` executes the static gate on the host. Because `check.py` unconditionally calls `runpy.run_path()` upon completing AST checks, the unsandboxed payload executes entirely on the host before `bwrap` is invoked, bypassing all intended OS sandboxing.

findings.title: np.load AST check fails open for non-constant arguments
findings.desc: The new gate requires `node.args[2]` to evaluate truthfully as an `ast.Constant` string/bool to throw a rejection. If an attacker passes a variable (parsed as `ast.Name`), the `isinstance` check resolves to False, bypassing the RCE protection entirely and allowing deserialization.

findings.title: Runtime patching in check.py fails to contain file writes or network
findings.desc: The decision documentation mandates that script-driven limits block network egress and unbound writes. While `check.py` correctly monkeypatches OS execution paths for the fallback tier, it omits patching `builtins.open` and network modules like `socket`, leaving writes to the host filesystem completely unchecked by the Python layer.

findings.title: bwrap tmpfs mapping obscures caller PWD causing chdir to fail
findings.desc: Mapping `/tmp` to an empty tmpfs eclipses the host environment. If the user invokes Claude Code from a directory sitting underneath `/tmp`, `bwrap`'s subsequent `--chdir "$PWD"` flag will target a now-nonexistent filesystem path, forcibly crashing the sandbox.

findings.title: AST gate bypass via allowed attributes

findings.title: Arbitrary host file write on fallback tier via `open()`
findings.desc: The AST gate's static verification of `open()` read-only mode was removed on the assumption runtime layers block writes. However, the Python-level runtime neutering in `check.py` only wraps `os.remove`-style ops, leaving `builtins.open`/`io.open` unpatched for arbitrary file overwrites via the fallback tier.

findings.title: Pickling RCE bypass in `np.load` positional/kwargs check
findings.desc: The `np.load` pickle check fails closed only if passing a truthy literal; providing a variable via the 3rd positional argument (e.g. `isinstance(args[2], ast.Constant)` resolves False) or leveraging kwargs (e.g., `**{"allow_pickle": True}`) bypasses the security gate enabling RCE.

findings.title: Sandbox start failure when execution runs within `/tmp`
findings.desc: When the script executes under `bwrap`, mapping `--tmpfs /tmp` masks any non-bound parent paths in `/tmp`. If Claude's working directory (`$PWD`) is under `/tmp`, the subsequent `--chdir "$PWD"` fails immediately with an ENOENT error, hard-crashing the invocation.

findings.desc: By relaxing the 3rd positional argument check to strictly filter for a truthy `ast.Constant`, evaluation completely fails open if an attacker passes a variable (e.g. `np.load(f, mode, my_var)`), while `**kwargs` unpacking is also ignored entirely, bypassing RCE protections.

findings.title: Pre-sandbox host compromise via AST verification phase
findings.desc: `check.py` unconditionally executes user code locally via `runpy.run_path()` during static verification. By removing AST blocks on `open()` and process execution names here, untrusted code will overwrite host files (via unpatched `builtins.open`) and execute commands (e.g. via `importlib.reload(os).system()`) on the host machine before `bwrap` restricts it.

findings.title: Bwrap crashes when executing from within host's `/tmp`
findings.desc: Mounting an empty tempfs over `/tmp` while explicitly keeping the host working path with `--chdir "$PWD"` guarantees that `bwrap` will crash with a missing directory error (and degrade the runtime sandbox) for callers whose workspaces reside inside `/tmp`.
